correctness.rationale: The theorem checks with a small proof correction, but the frozen Step 3 makes a false graph identification. Deleting E_(n−j) only for 1≤j<m leaves E_n as well as E_0,…,E_m; at n=4 it leaves six vertices instead of the asserted five. The frozen program's survivor list already omits E_n, but its twin assertions skip j=0, so its log is not evidence for the literal written step. The missing justification is that rim incompatibility reduces to residues differing by ±1 modulo n, with spoke neighbors s_b,s_(b+1) depending only on the residue b. Thus E_j and E_(n−j) are nonadjacent false twins for 0≤j<m, including E_0,E_n; deleting one from each pair gives the path of triangles with tip {s_(-j),s_(j+1)} adjacent to the two successive path vertices. False-twin removal preserves I(−1), and summing over tips leaves exactly the two alternating path selections. The signed Lefschetz factor is (−1)^(d+1) times I(−1), yielding the stated edge trace. The vertex trace is zero because the fixed s_0 has no admissible incident rim orbit. Over Q, averaging the barycentrically subdivided quotient chains gives the invariant homology and the stated ranks. Independent bounded replay checked actual face traces at n=4,6,8,10 and all twin pairs and the corrected adjacency at even n=4,…,40: python3 /workspace/checks/frozen_review_checks.py reflection.
